title: W4 fix is wrong for production data: the 'Form opened' timeline line is sorted lexically across MIXED timestamp formats, so it still misorders against same-day attempts (PG ::text 'space' form sorts before RFC3339 'T' form at index 10 regardless of clock time)
evidence: Sort key: list.sort(fn(a, b) { string.compare(a.at, b.at) }). Attempts' at-values are RFC3339 from sweep now_iso (sweep.gleam:178 timestamp.to_rfc3339, e.g. "2026-08-01T10:00:00Z"); form_opened_at is PG now()::text (list_reference_calls_for_detail.sql COALESCE(form_opened_at::text,'')), e.g. "2026-08-01 14:00:00+00" — the space shape is pinned on the wire by the new integration test (reference_detail_payload_integration_test.gleam:307 asserts "form_opened_at":"2026-08-01 21:12:00+00"). At index 10, ' ' (0x20) < 'T' (0x54), so any same-day PG-form timestamp sorts before any RFC3339 attempt at ANY hour that day. Simulated: lines [Invitation sent 2026-08-01T10:00:00Z, Form opened 2026-08-01 14:00:00+00] sort to [Form opened 14:00, Invitation sent 10:00]. The new test timeline_orders_form_opened_after_reminder_test (line 816) passes because its fixture is RFC3339-shaped (form_opened_at: Some("2026-08-03T18:00:00Z")) — not the production space shape — so it exercises a format mix that never ships and misses the defect.
detail: r1 W4 (warning, timeline-ordering) required the Form-opened line to be inserted chronologically against the attempts' at-values. The rework replaced the pinned-after-invite insertion with a sort whose comment claims 'lexical sort is chronological' — false for the payload's actual shapes. The most common case is affected: a referee who opens the link hours after the invite/reminder on the SAME day renders 'Form opened' ABOVE 'Invitation sent'/'Reminder n sent' in the mini timeline, contradicting the per-line <time datetime> values — the exact W4 complaint ('the line order then contradicts the per-line <time> datetimes') persists. Fix: normalize the sort key (e.g. reuse normalize_datetime on both sides, or sort on string.replace(at, " ", "T")), and pin the test with the production space-format fixture.
recommended_fix: Normalize form_opened_at to the RFC3339 'T' form before the lexical sort (the same normalization already applied to the datetime attribute), and change the timeline-ordering test fixture to the production PG ::text shape ('2026-08-03 18:00:00+00') so the mixed-format case is actually exercised.

title: W1 fix incomplete: the claimed no_em_dash_test extension never landed (copy_test.gleam untouched by the rework), and a shipped implementer-authored timeline label still contains an em-dash: 'Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}'
evidence: git diff 9d66ce9..e0f9fa7 -- client/test/copy_test.gleam is empty (0 changes across both rework commits 167a43b + e0f9fa7); no_em_dash_test at copy_test.gleam:308 still iterates only for_each_copy (toast/page codes), with zero refcheck references in copy_test.gleam. The two r1-flagged strings are genuinely fixed ('Unmoderated referee text: written by the referee, not reviewed by us.' and 'Applicant nudge: couldn't send' — both dash-free), but reference_panel.gleam:633 still ships copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail — an implementer-authored timeline label with an em-dash whose source does not exist in the UX spec (§7.6 shows no skipped-nudge line; the ban's guard names timeline labels explicitly as the banned class). The PR's own spec artifact documents the 'Skipped — {detail}' pattern, but that artifact is implementer-authored, not the UX source.
detail: The r1 W1 claimed fix was twofold ('Both rewritten without em-dashes; no_em_dash_test extended to scan refcheck consts'). The string rewrites landed; the regression guard did not, so CI would stay green if an em-dash returned to refcheck copy — and in fact one remains: the gate-skipped co-nudge timeline line renders 'Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}' (em-dash added by the implementer where the UX spec has no such line). Note the spec-verbatim dashes (sub-line, §7.4/§7.5/§7.8 copy, §10.3 confidence line, and the §7.6 wireframe 'Invitation sent — email + SMS' channel join at line 624) are correctly left in place — verbatim wins.
recommended_fix: Land the claimed test extension: scan the refcheck copy constants/compositions for em-dashes in a no_em_dash-style test, with an explicit allowlist for the spec-verbatim dash strings; and rewrite the nudge-skipped line without the implementer dash (e.g. 'Applicant nudge skipped: {detail}', matching the fixed nudge-failed line's colon style).
